## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `finished_at` column has to be fixed before merge: it holds the start time of processes that are still running, and the column documentation's NULL contract is also wrong.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `finished_at` column to the `processes` current-state model and documents it in `models/schema.yml`. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` file at the repository root.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Compute finished_at from a finish event, not 'started' — For process 20, whose latest event is `'started'`, `finished_at` is `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`, which is its start time. The `event_type` check constraint in `sources/process_events.sql:4` allows only `'created'`, `'started'` and `'cleared'`, so no finish event exists. — Consumers that read `finished_at` per `models/schema.yml:11` ("Timestamp when the process finished") will treat running processes as finished. — Fix: If the intent is a start timestamp, rename the column to `started_at` and update `models/schema.yml:9-11`; if the intent is a finish timestamp, decide which event marks completion before you expose the column.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Correct the NULL meaning in the finished_at description — Process 30 was `'started'` (event 3) and then `'cleared'` (event 4), so the `case` at `models/processes.sql:10` returns NULL for it. That contradicts "NULL means the process has never been started." — Consumers will wrongly treat every started process whose latest event is not `'started'` as never started.
